records.description: Two raw listing entries with the IDENTICAL (retailer, productUrl, price, size, variant, productId) tuple must collapse into ONE purchase option. This is a real, currently-shipped exact-identity mechanism — not a proposal.
records.notes: services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts optionFingerprint() (~line 174-183) + normalizePurchaseOptions()'s `seen` Set dedup (~line 189-260): this is real, shipped, exact-identity-based collapsing of literal duplicate listings — the one form of 'grouping' this app safely performs in production today. It is OFFER de-duplication (same exact listing seen twice), not cross-retailer PRODUCT grouping — see group-safe-hypothetical-cross-retailer-exact-id below for why that distinction matters.

records.description: IF a governed, cross-retailer-comparable exact product identifier existed (it does not, in production, today — see Finding F2), grouping two DIFFERENT retailers' offers under one product by that exact ID would be safe. This fixture demonstrates what safe cross-retailer grouping WOULD look like, using a clearly-labeled hypothetical field, so Commerce V2 has a concrete target shape to build toward without this corpus fabricating that the capability exists now.
records.notes: SYNTHETIC BOUNDARY DEMONSTRATION ONLY. Field name 'hypotheticalTrustedProductId' is deliberately not a real field name from any production type, to avoid this fixture being mistaken for evidence that GTIN-based grouping exists. This is the counterexample to must-not-group's canonicalProductKey-shaped cases: the difference between a SAFE grouping mechanism and the UNSAFE one that exists in source (Finding F2) is exact-ID-based vs. fuzzy-title-based matching.
